title: The ark is sent on to Ekron — the Greek names Ascalon (Askelon)
summary: The KJV says the Philistines sent the ark to Ekron (5:10) and that the five lords returned to Ekron (6:16). The Hebrew prints עֶקְרוֹן in both verses. Brenton’s Greek prints Ἀσκάλωνα (Ascalon) in both.
text:
Preserved draft text:
KJV 1 Samuel 5:10: “Therefore they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, as the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, saying, They have brought about the ark of the God of Israel to us, to slay us and our people.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 5:10: וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֛וּ אֶת־אֲרֹ֥ון הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עֶקְרֹ֑ון וַיְהִ֗י כְּבֹ֨וא אֲרֹ֤ון הָאֱלֹהִים֙ עֶקְרֹ֔ון וַיִּזְעֲק֨וּ הָֽעֶקְרֹנִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר הֵסַ֤בּוּ אֵלַי֙ אֶת־אֲרֹון֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לַהֲמִיתֵ֖נִי וְאֶת־עַמִּֽי׃ [and they sent the ark of God to Ekron; and it happened, when the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 5:10: Καὶ ἐξαποστέλλουσι τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα· καὶ ἐγενήθη ὡς εἰσῆλθε κιβωτὸς Θεοῦ εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα, καὶ ἐβόησαν οἱ Ἀσκαλωνῖται, λέγοντες, τί ἀπεστρέψατε τὴν κιβωτὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Ἰσραὴλ πρὸς ἡμᾶς θανατῶσαι ἡμᾶς καὶ τὸν λαὸν ἡμῶν; [and they send away the ark of God to Ascalon; and when the ark of God came into Ascalon, the Ascalonites cried out]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 5:10: “And they send away the ark of God to Ascalon; and it came to pass when the ark of God went into Ascalon, that the men of Ascalon cried out, saying, Why have ye brought back the ark of the God of Israel to us, to kill us and our people?” KJV 1 Samuel 6:16: “And when the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.” Hebrew (WLC) 1 Samuel 6:16: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה סַרְנֵֽי־פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים רָא֑וּ וַיָּשֻׁ֥בוּ עֶקְרֹ֖ון בַּיֹּ֥ום הַהֽוּא׃    ס [and the five lords of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ekron on that day]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 6:16: Καὶ οἱ πέντε σατράπαι τῶν ἀλλοφύλων ἑώρων, καὶ ἀνέστρεψαν εἰς Ἀσκάλωνα τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ. [and the five satraps of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ascalon on that day]. Brenton English 1 Samuel 6:16: “And the five lords of the Philistines saw, and returned to Ascalon in that day.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA05.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/5/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA05.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA05.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1SA06.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/9/6/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1SA06.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1SA06.htm.

reasoning:
Preserved draft reasoning:
In both verses the Hebrew reads Ekron and the Greek reads Ascalon, so the Greek tradition sends the ark, and the lords, to a different Philistine city. In the Greek the same chapter’s list of golden emerods (6:17) names both Ascalon and Accaron (Ekron), so a reader of the Greek has Ascalon as the third city of the ark’s journey and Accaron as the last city in the list.

New draft supplemental reasoning (reported, unverified):
The Hebrew edition quoted prints עֶקְרוֹן at 5:10 (three times) and at 6:16, where the five lords return to Ekron. The Greek printed at those verses prints Ἀσκάλωνα. At 6:17 the same Greek prints both Ἀσκάλωνος and Ἀκκαρών in its list of five cities, and the Hebrew prints both אַשְׁקְלוֹן and עֶקְרוֹן; so both texts name two cities in the list but differ in the narrative verses.

title: “The judge shall judge him” — the Greek has “they shall pray for him to the Lord”
summary: The KJV has Eli say, “If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him”. The Hebrew is וּפִלְלוֹ אֱלֹהִים. Brenton’s Greek reads καὶ προσεύξονται ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πρὸς Κύριον, “and they shall pray for him to the Lord”.

Preserved draft text:
KJV 1 Samuel 2:25: “If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him: but if a man sin against the Lord, who shall intreat for him? Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1 Samuel 2:25: Ἐὰν ἁμαρτάνων ἁμάρτῃ ἀνὴρ εἰς ἄνδρα, καὶ προσεύξονται ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πρὸς Κύριον· καὶ ἐὰν τῷ Κυρίῳ ἁμάρτῃ, τίς προσεύξεται ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ; Καὶ οὐκ ἤκουον τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτῶν, ὅτι βουλόμενος ἐβούλετο Κύριος διαφθεῖραι αὐτούς. [if a man sins against a man, they shall pray for him to the Lord; and if he sins against the Lord, who shall pray for him?]. title: Why the men of Bethshemesh were smitten — the Greek adds “the sons of Jechonias were not pleased”
summary: The KJV says the Lord smote the men of Bethshemesh “because they had looked into the ark of the Lord”. The Hebrew says כִּי רָאוּ בַּאֲרוֹן יְהוָה, “because they saw into the ark of the LORD”. Brenton’s Greek opens with a different clause: οὐκ ἠσμένισαν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰεχονίου ἐν τοῖς ἀνδράσι Βαιθσαμύς, “the sons of Jechonias were not pleased with the men of Bethshemesh”, and then adds “because they saw the ark of the Lord”.

summary: The KJV says David and his men, “which were about six hundred”, left Keilah. The Hebrew prints כְּשֵׁשׁ־מֵאוֹת אִישׁ, “about six hundred men”. Brenton’s Greek prints ὡς τετρακόσιοι, “about four hundred”.
